claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy is eutectic and has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The strength and plasticity of the starting alloy are below industrial application requirements.
A 70% room-temperature cold-rolling reduction followed by aging at 450°C for 6 hours will refine the lamellar spacing.
The proposed aging treatment will induce controlled nanoprecipitation at the lamellar interfaces.
Lamellar refinement and interfacial nanoprecipitation will produce ultrafine-grained regions.
The ultrafine-grained regions will hinder dislocation motion.
Severe plastic deformation from cold rolling will refine the alloy microstructure.
Cold-rolling-induced microstructural refinement will enhance yield strength through Hall–Petch strengthening.
Aging at 450°C for 6 hours will generate precipitates that impede dislocation motion.
Precipitation-induced impediment of dislocation motion will reduce room-temperature creep.
The aging treatment will stabilize grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary stabilization will mitigate degradation during temperature cycling from -40°C to 250°C.
The treatment will reduce microstructural sites susceptible to localized corrosion.
The treated alloy will have higher strength than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have greater ductility than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have lower room-temperature creep rate than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have a lower corrosion rate than the untreated alloy in saline or similarly corrosive environments.
The predicted benefits apply to fastener service involving temperature cycling from -40°C to 250°C, long-term static loading at room temperature, and corrosive exposure.

contradictions.description: The 70% rolling plus 450°C/6 h schedule is described as optimized, while the uncertainty field says the precise aging parameters remain uncertain and may require fine-tuning.
